# Loose Ends

> Loose Ends is a one-person studio run by Houssem Gabsi. It builds websites, automation and content systems for established firms, in English, French and Arabic.

Works with firms in the US and Europe, in English, French and Arabic.

Site: https://houssem-gabsi.vercel.app/

## Services

- Websites and applications.: The site clients judge the firm by and the tools the team opens every morning, designed and built end to end.
- Work that runs without anyone doing it.: Follow-up, confirmations and reports happen on their own. A person approves what matters before anything is sent.
- Identity and content.: A visual identity, and a content process that turns one idea into a week of publishing in the firm's own voice.

## Cases

Client work. Clients are not named.

### Open roles entered once, live everywhere.

Executive search, Washington D.C.

Roles go into the firm's recruiting system and appear on its eighteen-page website without anyone retyping them. Candidate CVs are put into the firm's format in one step. The same database now answers the team's questions through their AI assistant.

Status: Website live. Candidate scoring in development.

### A nineteenth-century house that looks like itself online.

Maison d'hôte, La Marsa

An identity drawn by hand from the house's own tiles, doors and objects. It runs through a website in French and English and the printed pieces guests hold, from the room card to the table d'hôte menu.

Status: Identity and print delivered. Website in development.

### A class booked on one screen, not in a message thread.

Yoga studio

Schedule, places and payment sit on a single phone screen, in French and English. Bookings moved out of Instagram messages and into one place.

Status: Live.

### An AI assistant that works the way he does.

Journalist, video production

His assistant is set up around his editorial week, not the software's defaults. The tasks he repeats now run the same way every time, with video production at the centre.

Status: Delivered 2026.

## Products

### Candidates ranked, with the reasoning behind every score.

The platform reads a batch of résumés against a role and ranks the candidates. Every score shows its reasoning and the source text it came from. Outreach is drafted from each candidate's own work, and the decision stays with the recruiter.

Status: In use.

### A daily risk score for stocks, funds and crypto.

Each trading day, stocks, funds and cryptocurrencies are scored on how far the price has moved from its average, with an entry zone and a stop level. Past calls are published and graded. It is a scoring system, not financial advice.

Status: In use.

## Systems

- Every unanswered enquiry, found and drafted.: The system reads the inbox, quotes and invoices, finds what went quiet, and drafts each reply. Someone approves, then it sends. Status: Works with email, quotes and invoices.
- Every candidate read against the search.: Each candidate is assessed against that search's own criteria, with the reasoning written beside the score. The recruiter decides. Status: Works with the firm's recruiting system.
- One idea, a week of publishing.: A researched article and a week of posts from a single idea. Every figure is checked against a named source before it goes out. Status: Works with the blog, Substack, LinkedIn and Instagram.
- Interview notes in, client report out.: Raw notes become a finished report in the firm's format. Every rating points to its source, and gaps are flagged, never filled. Status: Works with interview notes and the firm's report template.
- An assistant that knows the firm's own data.: Claude or another assistant is connected to the firm's files, inbox and databases, so anyone on the team can ask a question and get the answer from the source. Status: Works with Claude connectors (MCP) and the firm's own tools.
- Bookings confirmed, reminded and rescheduled.: Clients book on one screen. Confirmations, reminders and changes go out on their own, and the calendar stays correct. Status: Works with the calendar, the booking page and payments.
- Every invoice followed up until it is paid.: Unpaid invoices are tracked and a polite reminder is drafted at each stage. Someone approves before anything is sent. Status: Works with the accounting tool and email.
- New clients onboarded without the paperwork chase.: Forms, documents and signatures are collected in one place, filed correctly, and the team is told when everything is in. Status: Works with forms, e-signature and shared drives.
- Weekly figures prepared before anyone asks.: Numbers are pulled from the tools the firm already uses into one dashboard, and a short summary goes to the people who need it. Status: Works with spreadsheets, databases and Slack.
- Orders, stock and listings kept in step.: Sales on one channel update stock and listings everywhere else, so nothing is sold twice and nothing is retyped. Status: Works with Shopify, Etsy and spreadsheets.
- A newsletter that assembles itself.: The week's articles, updates and links are gathered into a draft in the firm's voice, ready to review and send. Status: Works with Substack and the firm's email platform.
- Posts scheduled across every channel.: One approved piece of content is adapted and scheduled for each platform, with the calendar visible to the team. Status: Works with LinkedIn, Instagram and the content calendar.
- Meeting notes turned into actions.: Calls are summarised, decisions and next steps are recorded in the right system, and each owner is reminded. Status: Works with the calendar, call recordings and the CRM.
- Documents filed where they belong.: Incoming files are read, named and placed in the right folder or record, so nobody searches for them later. Status: Works with email, shared drives and the firm's database.
- A website that search engines and AI assistants can read.: Pages are structured so search results and assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity can find the firm, understand it and cite it. Status: Works with the website and its content.

## How an engagement starts

1. Find the loose end. A free one-page review of where the firm loses time. No call required.
2. Measure it. A paid audit ranks the first three fixes by what they return. The fee is credited toward the build.
3. Build one thing. The fix with the most hours in it, at one price agreed in writing.
